facts.text: Nehalem was named for the native Salishan word meaning place where people live, honoring the Tillamook people who traditionally inhabited the area.
The city of Nehalem thrived in the late nineteenth century as a hub for the logging, fishing, and shipping industries.
Nehalem has been a source of inspiration for various products, including a Nike sandal, a Leatherman knife, and an Intel microarchitecture.
The Portland-based band Everclear wrote a song called Nehalem about life in the town for their album Sparkle and Fade.
The Nehalem Bay Dune Site is a prehistoric location listed in the National Register of Historic Places dating back to 1310 A.D.
Nehalem sits at an elevation of only eleven feet, making the area prone to intermittent flooding from the river and ocean.
